A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same polymatrix-game equilibrium-finding work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including material relocated in v2.

before.justification: Section 9 and Figures 1–2 report original simulations measuring exploitability and privacy budgets on synthetic dense and sparse graphs.

after.justification: Section 9 and Appendix D report original simulations, including baseline comparisons and experiments on additional graph topologies.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same Gaussian-perturbed communications, simplex projections, degree-dependent regularization, and strategy updates. Renaming and clearer descriptions do not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's randomly generated dense and sparse graphs, v2 evaluates clustered dense graphs and spatial nearest-neighbor sparse graphs. Section 9 and Appendix D.1 substantially broaden the tested interaction structures while retaining the polymatrix-game task.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates only the proposed algorithm. v2 adds an evaluated baseline adapted from Huang et al. (2015), with comparison curves in Figures 3–8; that work was previously only cited.

E3.justification: The reported random-sparse-graph parameter changes from c=2,6,10 in v1 Figure 2 to c=1,3,5 in v2 Figure 6, while the captions retain the cN-edge construction. v2 also introduces explicitly matched privacy budgets for baseline comparisons. These are reported setting and control changes, without establishing which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a targeted topology check: clustered and spatial-neighbor graphs test whether the observed behavior persists beyond the original random constructions. This adds topology-robustness evidence, without introducing component ablations.

E5.justification: v1 already displays shaded bands but does not define them. v2 Appendix D explicitly states that error bars denote 1σ. Neither version specifies repeat counts or seeds, so an increase in runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: v2 adds baseline outcomes and results for clustered and spatial graphs. Its dense-graph comparisons report decreasing exploitability for the proposed method versus increasing baseline exploitability under matched privacy budgets. The earlier qualitative findings—improving dense-graph behavior and no clear sparse-graph exploitability decrease—remain.

T1.justification: The main theorem bounds and appendix proofs are largely retained. However, Section 8 adds different accuracy-rate expressions alongside the originals, including O((log N)^(1/3)/N^(4p/27)) in the sparse case beside the retained O((log N)^(-1/3)), without a corresponding new derivation. It also adds a non-private mirror-descent rate comparison.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the claimed algorithmic target from Nash equilibrium to coarse correlated equilibrium, aligning it with Section 5 in both versions. The abstract adds an explicit first-of-its-kind claim. The central impossibility and simultaneous vanishing privacy/exploitability claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets restricted adversarial access as a largely reliable communication network, distinguishes finite-iteration approximation error from convergence rate, and explicitly identifies extension beyond polymatrix games as a limitation and future direction. The explanation for weak sparse-graph empirical improvement is retained.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly reports execution on two NVIDIA H200 GPUs and specifies construction of the added clustered and spatial graphs. PyTorch implementation and selecting hyperparameters according to Theorem 8.1 were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds minimax-optimization literature and explains the distinction between protecting utility components and protecting the whole payoff function. It also adds decentralized-privacy and attack references. These broaden the discussion while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the exposition: convergence and privacy proof sketches move into Appendices B–C, Section 4 gains separate subsections and proof intuition, and the main experimental narrative becomes comparative with fuller results in Appendix D. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are also expanded.

P2.justification: v2 adds the conceptual illustration in Figure 1, redraws experimental plots with separate action-size panels and baseline curves, and adds clustered and spatial results. Dense-graph summaries appear in the main text while fuller plots occupy Appendix D. The payoff tables retain their substance.

improvement.justification: Matched-budget baseline comparisons, additional graph topologies, and clearer uncertainty reporting strengthen the empirical evidence. However, v2 introduces a visible 'TBD' in Theorem 6.1 and Appendix B, plus unreconciled additional accuracy-rate expressions in Section 8 while retaining the earlier proofs. These problems affect the central theoretical presentation, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
